summary.text: 方 is an ancient graph whose early uses include a western direction, the four directions, and polities. Its earliest shape is disputed: it has been read as a tool or blade, among other possibilities, while a later dictionary tradition interpreted it as paired boats. The shape alone does not settle its original referent.

formation.text: Pictographic analysis of the whole graph is possible, but its referent is unresolved. Competing interpretations include a marked blade or tool, other implements, and paired boats. The evidence does not support dividing 方 into historically meaningful internal components.

components.text: 方 is treated as one whole graph in the competing pictorial analyses; no internal component or component role is established.

history.text: The curated oracle-script-style image represents an early graphic candidate, but the competing readings do not establish what object it depicts. The paired-boats account belongs to a later dictionary tradition; the curated seal-script-style image illustrates that tradition, not proof of the graph’s original referent.

Oracle and bronze forms are reported as broadly similar, with variation in upper strokes. A later account describes transformation in the seal form and clerical writing as the basis for later forms; the evidence does not show that every graphic difference was a corruption.

uncertainties.text: The early graph’s referent remains disputed among blade-, tool-, implement-, paddle-, and boat-related interpretations. No proposed object-name or pronunciation is independently established, so the proposed borrowing of 方 for “square” through sound similarity remains a hypothesis.

The reported early and later uses do not establish a dated sequence linking direction, polity or region, square, method, and temporal “just/now.” Individual early examples lack precise dates in the supplied evidence.
A proposed connection with 旁 does not establish that 方 was its original graph or that the words share meaning; reported historical sound similarity permits only a possible phonetic relation.

senses.gloss: direction, including west and the four quarters
senses.text: Reported Shang inscription uses include a western-direction context and 四方. These attestations establish early directional use, but do not show whether it continues the graph’s original meaning or reflects borrowing for a similar-sounding word.
Reported Shang examples use 方 for polities and polity leaders. Their relationship to the directional use is not established.

A Western Zhou bronze example is reported with the square sense. One scholarly analysis proposes that the graph was borrowed for this word from a separate object-name because the two words sounded alike or similar. The object-name and sound match are unknown, so this borrowing account is not demonstrated.
A Western Zhou bronze example is reported for land measurement; the evidence does not establish how this use relates to the square, direction, or polity senses.
Later lexicographic records include method and law. The available evidence does not date their emergence or connect them in a secure semantic sequence to the earlier attested uses.
A period-labeled bronze example is glossed “just/now.” The evidence does not establish its development from another sense.

senses.period: late Warring States to early Qin context
senses.text: A Shuihudi Qin slip is reported to use 方 for a writing board. This is a recorded use, with no established semantic link to the other senses.
These are supplied modern glosses; their listing does not establish when or how each sense developed.

developments.text: Both uses are reported in Shang material, but the evidence does not establish whether the polity use developed from the directional sense or was written with the same graph through sound borrowing.

One analysis proposes that the graph was reused for the word “square” because it sounded like the name of the depicted object. Since that name and sound comparison are unavailable, the proposed borrowing mechanism remains unverified and its timing is unresolved.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a complete semantic chronology or connect the recorded square, measurement, region, method, and temporal senses into a single chain.
The earliest depicted object and any borrowing based on its name remain unresolved; the supplied historical pronunciations are readings of 方, not records of the depicted object’s name.

overview.text: 方 is an ancient graph used for directions and polities in reported Shang inscriptions. Its early shape may picture a tool or implement, but the referent is disputed; a later dictionary tradition interpreted it as paired boats.

components.text: Treat 方 as one whole graph: the evidence offers competing pictures of its early form, not a supported breakdown into smaller parts.

takeaway.text: The proposed link between an early object and “square” depends on an unknown object-name and an unverified sound match.
